messages:
maria: quick sync — we need a concrete plan for rollout/canary/A-B metrics + dashboards. goal: comparative panels that surface regressions (latency/error/cost) and actionable signals for rollbacks. anyone free?
kevin: I can drive the runtime instrumentation. what's the minimum metric set we should emit from the serving runtime?
suzanne: minimum list from observability POV: p95/p99 latency, error_rate (by error class), success_rate, throughput (req/s), kv_cache_hit_rate, batching_rate, token_cost_per_request, fallback_rate. plus histogram buckets for latency.
anil: infra adds: gpu_util, queue_depth, oom_count, kernel_slowdown_ms, mean_batch_size. these help explain perf regressions vs model issues.
eva: product asks for comparative UI requirements: show canary vs baseline side-by-side, delta (abs + %), sample sizes, and CI/p_value. also surface business signals: error_budget_burn, cost_delta_per_1k_tokens, and SLA_violations.
kevin: proposed metric naming + tags (snippet):
```
redwood.runtime.latency.p95{model="mistral-8x",deployment="canary",route="chat",region="us-west-2"}
redwood.runtime.errors.rate{error_class="oom",model=...,deployment=...}
redwood.runtime.kv_cache.hit_rate{model=...,deployment=...}
redwood.runtime.request.info_count{batch_size=...,seq_len=...,routing_policy=...}
```
keep tags: model, deployment, route, region, customer_tier. avoid high-card tags like user_id.
maria: UX: rollout page should show a small banner/scorecard with overall pass/fail, and a rollback CTA if regression above threshold. per-route drilldown and link to traces/logs. also show traffic split and model_variant_ratio.
suzanne: for alerts: compute relative uplift = (canary - baseline)/baseline. signal when p95 uplift > 10% AND p_value < 0.05. suggest bootstrap CI for percentiles; require min sample size e.g. 1k reqs per cohort for latency signals.
anil: runtime needs to emit per-request lightweight metadata: model_id, seq_len_bucket, batch_size_bucket, routing_policy, cache_hit boolean, fallback boolean. QPS is high so default to 10% sampling for full request tags + 100% for counters/aggregates. we should also emit histograms (HDR) to avoid expensive cardinality.
kevin: agree on sampling. we'll emit aggregated counters for total_requests, error_counts, token_cost_sum with tags, and sampled request-level events for histograms/traces. also recommend using prometheus histograms for latency + t-digest for long-term analysis.
sally: analytics can build the comparative dashboard. plan: summary row (delta_p95, delta_error_rate, p_value, sample_sizes, cost_diff), time-series panels (baseline vs canary overlay), and distribution panels (latency CDFs). we can compute p_value via bootstrap job running on metrics ingestion (not realtime).
suzanne: tag taxonomy reminder: include route, team, customer_tier, model_variant, region, deployment_config. avoid adding customer or user ids.
maria: timeline check — we need MVP on dashboards by next week's release freeze. realistic?
kevin: instrumentation PRs this week (2 engineers). dashboard skeleton + queries next week. alerting + auto-rollbacks will be phase 2.
anil: flags: don't add too many tag dimensions in runtime counters — high cardinality causes TSDB pain. sample more heavily for uncommon routes. also confirm retention/cost for raw sampled events.
eva: I'll write acceptance criteria for rollout UX (what counts as pass/fail, threshold defaults, how CTA behaves).
kevin: small implementation detail: use metric name prefix "redwood.runtime." and a field "deployment=canary|baseline|control" so panels can easily aggregate.
sally: for A/B tests, we need cohort ids emitted so we can join business metrics later. emit cohort_id at sampled rate only.
suzanne: we'll add dashboard panels that show both relative % and absolute diffs; highlight when absolute latency increase exceeds 100ms even if % is small.
maria: action items: 1) kevin + anil: RFC + PR for runtime instrumentation (include sampling plan, tag list, metric names). 2) suzanne + sally: prototype dashboard panels + queries. 3) eva: rollout UX acceptance criteria. 4) kevin: add example dashboards/alerts to repo. target: instrumentation merged by Thu, dashboard draft by Tue.
kevin: I'll open the RFC this afternoon and ping folks. linking notes in #eng-docs.
suzanne: I'll mock panels in Grafana and share a link.
nana: :thinking_face: (typo)
maria: :thumbsup: thanks all — I'll follow up with a short checklist and assign owners in Asana.
deploy-bot: canary started for deployment canary-2026-03-18-v1 — tracking id abc123
kevin: noted, will add monitoring for that canary specifically (temp dashboard).
sally: once dashboard prototype exists I can wire up the cohort joins for business metrics.
anil: one more: log a schema migration ticket for telemetry to infra board — we need to bump ingestion quotas.
maria: ok closing thread for now. ping here when PRs/links posted.
